implementation_notes: C accumulates lava flow in the build: a project that links both libxml2 wrappers and its own parser, or both an event library and a hand-rolled thread pool, with both used in different subsystems written by different generations. Because linking is a build-time property and there is no type-level notion of a duplicate capability, the two coexist silently for years. Detection is the link map plus a count of implementations per capability; the mitigation is a compile-time or link-time rule that forbids both, since a header that pulls in both is a reviewable failure. The removal question is the usual one — what still calls the old one — and here `-Wl,--gc-sections` and symbol maps give real answers.
idiom_name: two C libraries for the same job, both linked
pitfalls: A vendored copy of a library alongside a system copy means the dependency survives any package upgrade.
Header-level reimplementation inside a project directory looks like a wrapper but is usually a fork that nobody remembers starting.
Link-time selection can be made at build time only if the rule is written down; otherwise the default is coexistence.
